case_name: Union Of India And Another v Mahajabeen Akhtar
respondent:
Mahajabeen Akhtar
Supreme Court of India

1 November 2007
Appeal (civil) 5087 of 2007 (ARISING OUT OF SLP (C) NO. 6635 OF 2005)
The Judgment was delivered by: S. B. Sinha, J.
Leave granted.
1.  Applicability of the doctrine of  equal pay for equal work  is in question in this appeal which arises out of a judgment and order dated 19.08.2004 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court of Delhi in Civil Writ Petition No.3719 of 2002 dismissing the writ petition filed by the appellant questioning an order dated 11.9.2000 passed in Original Application No.52 of 2000 by the Central Administrative Tribunal directing to consider the question of grant of replacement pay scale of Rs.6500 10500 to the respondent, with consequential benefits in her favour.
Basic fact of the matter is not in dispute.
2.  Respondent herein was appointed as Technical Assistant of Urdu Language in the Bureau of Promotion of Urdu Language. She was placed in the pay scale of Rs.425 700. She
facts: The respondent was appointed as Technical Assistant of Urdu Language in the Bureau of Promotion of Urdu Language.
She was placed in the pay scale of Rs.425-700 and later promoted to Research Assistant in the scale of pay of Rs.550-900.
Her name was referred to surplus cell for redeployment after NCPUL started functioning from 1.4.1996.
The respondent opted for Government service and her pay was upgraded in the scale of Rs.6500-10500.
issues: Applicability of the doctrine of equal pay for equal work
petitioner_arguments: The Tribunal and consequently the High Court committed a serious error in arriving at the aforementioned conclusion in so far as they failed to take into consideration the fact that the nature of qualification and other relevant factors clearly point out that the post of Librarian is not equivalent to that of the post of Research Assistant in other regional languages.
respondent_arguments: As the respondent had been in the job of the Bureau of Promotion of Urdu Language as on 1.1.1996 from which date the recommendations of the Fifth Pay Commission came to be implemented, the impugned judgment and order should not be interfered with.
court_reasoning: The Tribunal held that all the institutes including BPU were functioning on 01.01.1996 when the recommendations of the 5th Pay Commission were implemented.
There is no reason why the Research Assistant in BPU should have been treated in a different matter.
holding: The impugned judgment and order are accordingly affirmed and petition is disposed of.
